messages.author: ac19819864ba3828
messages.subject: Plot subsets of data, in a loop
parts:
Hi,

>> Overview
I want to plot certain subsets of data, based on a certain condition, in a loop.

>> Attempt
Here is what I did so far:

#### Dummy Data ----
n = 500 # no of sample in each dist
n.d = 3 # no of dist
kind = c(LETTERS[1:n.d])
color.1 = "#7777DD"
color.2 = "#CC6666"
color.3 = "#ccbe66d1"
v.col = c(color.1,color.2,color.3)

df.1 <- data.frame(kind=rep(kind, each=n), x=c(rnorm(n, 1), rbeta(n, 1,1), runif(n)), my.col = rep(v.col,each=n))
#### `````````````````````````````````````````````````````

####  Main ----
l.1 = dlply(df.1,.(kind))

# Plot Function
fn.1 = function(df)
{
  ggplot() + geom_density(aes(x=x,fill=my.col), data=df, binwidth=0.2, position="identity", alpha=0.3) 
}

# Plots
my.plots = llply(l.1,fn.1)
#### `````````````````````````````````````````````````````

>> Problem
Everything works, except plots (my.plots[[1]], ...) are not filled with my.col. 

Following is what I tried, but cannot seem to iterate over  list of plots, and list of colors at the same time
llply(my.plots,function(p) p + scale_fill_manual(color.2)) ##  filling  with color.2, 


Any help will be appreciated. 


// Cheers ...

messages.subject: Re: Plot subsets of data, in a loop
parts: Unsure if you already received a reply, but this perhaps does what you need.

library(ggplot2)
#### Dummy Data ----
n = 500 # no of sample in each dist
n.d = 3 # no of dist
kind = c(LETTERS[1:n.d])
color.1 = "#7777DD"
color.2 = "#CC6666"
color.3 = "#ccbe66d1"
v.col = c(color.1,color.2,color.3)
df.1 <- data.frame(kind=rep(kind, each=n), x=c(rnorm(n, 1), rbeta(n, 1,1), runif(n)))

meanagg = aggregate(df.1$x, list(df.1$kind), mean)
meanlist=split(meanagg$x,rownames(meanagg))

# Plot Function
fn.1 = function(i){ggplot(df.1[which(df.1$kind==levels(df.1$kind)[[i]]),],aes(x=x)) + geom_density(binwidth=0.2, position="identity", fill=v.col[[i]],alpha=.3)+
                     geom_vline(aes(xintercept=meanlist[[i]]),linetype="dashed", size=0.5)}

# generate list of plots
my.plots=vector('list',length=n.d)
for (i in 1:n.d){my.plots[[i]]=fn.1(i)}
for (i in 1:n.d){print(my.plots[[i]])}
Vivek

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Plot subsets of data, in a loop
parts:
I'm assuming you want different colors for each density plot and a
single mean line for each estimated density. Two versions are
provided: a faceted version (all on one graphic) and a list version
(separate density plots). If I missed the point, then please clarify.

library(plyr)
library(ggplot2)

n = 500 # no of sample in each dist
n.d = 3 # no of dist
kind = c(LETTERS[1:n.d])
color.1 = "#7777DD"
color.2 = "#CC6666"
color.3 = "#ccbe66d1"
v.col = c(color.1,color.2,color.3)

df.1 <- data.frame(kind=rep(kind, each=n), x=c(rnorm(n, 1), rbeta(n,
1,1), runif(n)), my.col = rep(v.col,each=n))

# Group means
df.mean = ddply(df.1,.(kind),summarise,my.mean=mean(x))

# Faceted version

ggplot(df.1, aes(x = x, fill = my.col)) +
geom_density(color = NA) +
geom_vline(data = df.mean, aes(xintercept = my.mean), linetype = "dashed") +
facet_wrap(~ kind, scales = "free") +
labs(x = NULL, color = "kind", fill = "kind") +
scale_fill_identity(labels = levels(df.1$kind), guide = "legend")

# List version

# The plot function applies to a single 'kind', so the first few lines grab the
# appropriate data subsets from df.1 and df.mean. Since subset() uses
# non-standard evaluation rules, it's safer to use the brute force method
# of subsetting in the function body. Since color and fill are set in
# geom_density, no legend is produced.

g <- function(grp)
{
d1 <- df.1[df.1$kind == grp, ]
dm <- df.mean[df.mean$kind == grp, ]
my.col <- unique(as.character(d1$my.col))

p <- ggplot(d1, aes(x = x)) +
geom_density(color = NA, fill = my.col) +
geom_vline(data = dm, aes(xintercept = my.mean),
linetype = "dashed") +
labs(x = NULL)
p
}

L <- as.character(levels(df.1$kind))

# Generate the plot objects, put them into a list
plotlist <- llply(L, g)

# Print them individually
print(plotlist[[1]])
print(plotlist[[2]])
print(plotlist[[3]])


Dennis

On Fri, Jan 31, 2014 at 3:35 AM, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm assuming you want different colors for each density plot and a
single mean line for each estimated density. Two versions are
provided: a faceted version (all on one graphic) and a list version
(separate density plots). If I missed the point, then please clarify.

library(plyr)
library(ggplot2)

n = 500 # no of sample in each dist
n.d = 3 # no of dist
kind = c(LETTERS[1:n.d])
color.1 = "#7777DD"
color.2 = "#CC6666"
color.3 = "#ccbe66d1"
v.col = c(color.1,color.2,color.3)

df.1 <- data.frame(kind=rep(kind, each=n), x=c(rnorm(n, 1), rbeta(n,
1,1), runif(n)), my.col = rep(v.col,each=n))

# Group means
df.mean = ddply(df.1,.(kind),summarise,my.mean=mean(x))

# Faceted version

ggplot(df.1, aes(x = x, fill = my.col)) +
   geom_density(color = NA) +
   geom_vline(data = df.mean, aes(xintercept = my.mean), linetype = "dashed") +
   facet_wrap(~ kind, scales = "free") +
   labs(x = NULL, color = "kind", fill = "kind") +
   scale_fill_identity(labels = levels(df.1$kind), guide = "legend")

# List version

# The plot function applies to a single 'kind', so the first few lines grab the
# appropriate data subsets from df.1 and df.mean. Since subset() uses
# non-standard evaluation rules, it's safer to use the brute force method
# of subsetting in the function body. Since color and fill are set in
# geom_density, no legend is produced.

g <- function(grp)
{
    d1 <- df.1[df.1$kind == grp, ]
    dm <- df.mean[df.mean$kind == grp, ]
    my.col <- unique(as.character(d1$my.col))

    p <- ggplot(d1, aes(x = x)) +
            geom_density(color = NA, fill = my.col) +
            geom_vline(data = dm, aes(xintercept = my.mean),
                                  linetype = "dashed") +
            labs(x = NULL)
    p
}

L <- as.character(levels(df.1$kind))

# Generate the plot objects, put them into a list
plotlist <- llply(L, g)

# Print them individually
print(plotlist[[1]])
print(plotlist[[2]])
print(plotlist[[3]])


Dennis
